answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted voting: an agent earns influence only by locking real collateral, not by possessing a name. Imagine a shared garden where a vote counts only if you drive a timber post and seal it with an ivory marker you had to pay for. An attacker who splits into a thousand fake agents still must buy a thousand posts and markers, with no discount for quantity. Because that collateral is locked and slashed when fraud is detected, the cost of the attack rises linearly with every new identity, so a large sybil farm becomes unprofitable.
